verdict.note: Measured through the adoption path on a fresh repository, not through the handler alone. `git init` + one source file + `spex init --harness claude` in a clean HOME: the hooks materialize with the access trigger (`hp_code_path "$payload" access`), and the claude shim is written with the compiled entry. Governing one file with a `code:` claim and firing the materialized PreToolUse dispatch with a Write against it blocks once — "Before accessing governed source app.ts, read its governing spec FIRST: .spec/project/app/spec.md [app]" — and the identical retry passes, so the gate stays one-shot. This is the half of the trigger that has now been dropped twice; before this change the same Write produced no block at all. Unit matrix in hook-dispatch.test.ts 34/34 (both harnesses, governed write, ungoverned write, ungoverned-then-governed, one-shot).
